LandingPage.intro1: Music that truly moves people usually carries several layers at once: precise rhythmic structure (the physical layer), rigorously considered arrangement logic (the structural layer), depth that confronts emotional ups and downs (the emotional layer), and dynamic tension held in balance (the vital layer).
LandingPage.intro2: Computable Beauty tries to translate this four-dimensional aesthetic intuition into computable, verifiable dimensions.

extracting.label: Acoustic Feature Extraction
extracting.detail: Computes spectrum, beat grid, key/pitch distribution, and dynamic envelope from the waveform, producing the base feature vector for later analysis

classifying.label: Multi-Task Semantic Classification
classifying.detail: Infers genre, valence/arousal, and instrumentation in parallel, while detecting chord progressions, key, and section boundaries

scoring.label: Four-Dimensional Aesthetic Scoring
scoring.detail: Quantifies physical precision, structural logic, emotional depth, and vital tension based on the acoustic and classification results, combining them into an overall aesthetic index

explaining.label: AI Evidence-Based Interpretation
explaining.detail: An LLM generates a written analysis grounded in the structured output of the previous layers, with every conclusion traceable back to a specific metric

physical_precision.label: Physical
physical_precision.description: Quantifies the physical precision of performance and production from signal features like tempo stability, spectral energy distribution, and dynamic range.

structural_logic.label: Logic
structural_logic.description: Measures whether the music's structure forms a coherent whole, based on harmonic progression patterns, section duration ratios, and tonal stability.

emotional_depth.label: Emotion
emotional_depth.description: Measures the completeness of emotional movement from the peak-to-valley range of the emotional arc, the number of polarity shifts, and the dispersion of arousal.

vital_tension.label: Vitality
vital_tension.description: Measures the intensity of tension between opposing elements from loudness dynamic contrast, the frequency of energy shifts, and the proportion of dissonant harmonic intervals.

EvidenceLabel.tempo_stability: Tempo Stability (BPM variance, lower = more stable)
EvidenceLabel.frequency_balance: Spectral Balance (low/mid/high frequency energy ratio, more balanced = higher)
EvidenceLabel.dynamic_range_db: Loudness Envelope Range (difference between max and min RMS, in dB)
EvidenceLabel.spectral_entropy: Timbre Complexity Proxy (mean entropy of the mel spectrogram, higher = richer)
EvidenceLabel.tsd_coverage: T-S-D Function Coverage (chord sequence analysis, higher = more conventional)
EvidenceLabel.segment_balance: Section Duration Balance (structural segment durations, closer to 1 = more balanced)
EvidenceLabel.key_stability: Key Change Frequency & Resolution (tonal analysis, higher = more stable)
EvidenceLabel.valence_delta: Emotional Arc Range (difference between the arc's max and min)
EvidenceLabel.polarity_switches: Emotional Polarity Shift Density (positive/negative flips between adjacent frames)
EvidenceLabel.arousal_std: Arousal Dispersion (standard deviation of arousal values)
EvidenceLabel.high_arousal_ratio: High-Arousal Duration Ratio (share of segments with arousal above 0.6)
EvidenceLabel.dynamic_contrast: Loudness Dynamic Contrast (ratio of the loudest to the quietest section's RMS)
EvidenceLabel.burst_density: Energy Burst Frequency (number of local onset-strength maxima, per minute)
EvidenceLabel.silence_burst_ratio: Silence-to-Burst Ratio (silent frame duration vs. high-energy frame duration)
EvidenceLabel.dissonance_ratio: Harmonic Tension (proportion of dissonant chord intervals)

arousal.label: Arousal
arousal.description: The activation intensity dimension of emotion, reflecting the level of psychophysiological arousal — higher values indicate stronger physiological activation and alertness; lower values trend toward calm and relaxed.
arousal.computation: Jointly predicted by the emotion recognition model from acoustic features such as timbre, pitch, loudness, and rhythm.

valence.label: Valence
valence.description: The positive/negative polarity dimension of emotion, representing how pleasant the emotional experience is — positive values correspond to a positive, pleasant emotional tone, negative values to a negative, low tone, with 0 being neutral.
valence.computation: Shares the same acoustic features as arousal, jointly predicted by the same model.

tension.label: Tension
tension.description: The sense of instability and unresolvedness the music accumulates over time — higher values sound more suspended, anticipating resolution.
tension.computation: Derived from the overall output of the emotion recognition model; a standalone quantification method is still being refined.

release.label: Release
release.description: The sense of stability and closure once tension resolves — higher values indicate tension has been fully released, sounding settled and relaxed.
release.computation: Derived from the overall output of the emotion recognition model; a standalone quantification method is still being refined.

energy.label: Energy
energy.description: The overall drive and intensity of the music, jointly reflecting rhythmic density, dynamics, and timbre — higher values indicate stronger momentum and impact.
energy.computation: Derived from the overall output of the emotion recognition model; a standalone quantification method is still being refined.
